text: I've just finished playing the full campaign on Shadow Warrior. Thoroughly enjoyed it. It took me approx 20 hours play to get to the end. It is a fast First Person Shooter game in the style of DOOM, Quake, Unreal, Serious Sam, but with Melee weapon (Samurai sword) as well as the guns, rocket launcher, and other weapons. My rig has AMD FX 8350 processor, 16GB DDR3 RAM, and Nvidia GTX 1070 8GB graphics. I've been playing at 4K resolution and high graphics settings and the FPS has been good enough for me. I've been playing the game on Linux, and very grateful to the developers for releasing it on my preferred operating system. Waiting with high anticipation for the latest installment ( Shadow Warrior 2 ) to come to Linux. (The devs did say they were going to do it.) For a game that came out in 2013, it still looks very nice in 2017 (and 4K helps with that). I really liked many aspects of the game, because it is somewhat different to other FPS. The sword melee combat is cool. I'm liking the Powers and Skills and how those affect the use of the Sword. Liking the upgrades for the weapons. (You find money in the game and use that to pay towards upgrades.) The campaign story is interesting and adds to the enjoyment. Various Easter Egg secrets in the game are fun to spot and find, and nods to other games. Liking all the different types of baddies and how you have to adjust your play to face each type differently. Very happy to play it. It's *my* type of game. If you like this one, then you'll probably love Shadow Warrior 2, Serious Sam 3: BFE, and DOOM (2016)  - and vice versa.

text: I've been looking for a modern adaption of a fast paced, oldschool first-person shooter, comparable to Painkiller or Serious Sam. - Story: For a game of this niche the story is surprisingly entertaining. The basic idea: A man gets drawn into the conflict between demon lords and in pursuit of a legendary sword gets the power to not only save his world, but to also change the fate of their shadowy realm. There are a couple of nice looking comic sequences in which the background story is revealed piece by piece, where your sometimes a bit annoying companion becomes a more interesting character over time. Not bad! - Combat System: Fast and responsive. Melee is a big component and you unlock different swordstrikes over time. You have some magic spells (healing, stun, damage) and some enemies require different tactics. - Character System: You have three areas to improve; skills, magic and weapons. Each require a different currency to unlock. There certainly is some room for individual choices so it's not just a feature without purpose. - Presentation/Physics: Even two years after release, the game is still looking well enough. Enemies can be cut to pieces, burned or pushed away, some objects can be broken. The weapons feel strong and give a good impression of power in the game world. - Sound/Music: Just well made. Weapons and enemies sound good, music is decent - a few tracks with asian or jazz influence are even good. Can't complain. - Humour: It didn't make me break down laughing and did not send my sides into orbit. But still, the occasional Wang joke or light hearted comment was certainly good to keep the spirits high during the more repetitive moments of the game. - Hidden extras: Join the old-school fun when looking for the most inconspicuous places. Exploration is well rewarded with money (for weapons) and an XP like currency for skills. Contains some references to the original game aswell. - Difficulty: The highest setting "insane" felt just right for me as an experienced gamer. Enemies are dangerous and you have to be on your toes not to be surrounded my smaller minions or charged to death by the dreaded berserkers. Still, quicksave and the manual healing ability make every fight winnable. Even though you spend some time each fight just running away and healing yourself it still feels way better than those auto healing mechanics. - Weapons: Nothing really creative or particulary interesting. Katana, Revolver, SMG, Crossbow, Shotgun, Flamethrower, Rocket Launcher, Demon Heart, Demon Head. Each weapon can undergo at least one interesting change via upgrade. - Level design: Almost a negative point, if not for some beautiful places and those sometimes well hidden extras. Every now and then you re-visit areas that look very similar to other ones. Could be more diverse. Most fights have an arena like feeling where enemies are spawning until you've killed them all and the door to the next area opens. - Enemies: Nicely designed, some require special tactics. They get repetitive over time though. A plus are the big boss battles, although they all play VERY similar. Cool design though. - Characters: Not many interesting characters, which only develop over time. Doesn't take itself too seriously though, which avoids mindnumbing stereotypes. - Repetitiveness: Consider this as a huge point. Some areas really feel drawn out, thanks to the arena fights and repetitive level design. There have been a couple of places where I was plain bored. - Bugs: I fell through the floor a couple of times and you can die when dashing down stairs. Minor annoyance. I've been pursuing this hobby since the mid 90s. My favorite genres are Strategy games, RPGs and (increasingly less) FPS. I also enjoy the occasional platformer, adventure or other indi game. I like competitive elements in online games, but without the social component of hanging out with friends I'd often prefer offline titles.

text: Shadowgrounds - it's good, very good. In a nutshell it's a total rip-off every single sci-fi horror movie with aliens in it, especially Aliens. You get to play a mechanic blasting your way through 11 levels of mayhem with a good variety of weapons with upgrades that will change how you use each weapon in different scenarios and also helps to cater for different styles of play. It's a top down shooter where you are investigating the strange going ons at the space station where you work. The game itself has been heavily influenced by the Aliens franchise and this is apparent in the unfolding storyline which wont win any awards and is very linear but serves it purpose for providing a good narrative to give you reason to pump alien♥♥♥♥♥full of lead. I myself totally loved the storyline - it's almost like an Aliens fanboy spinoff movie. As well as this there are very clear influences from seminal games of the past like Quake2 and there are quite a few other little influences in the game from movies and games of this genre but i will leave for you to spot them and not spoil it all for you. The graphics themselves are nothing to write home about but the awesome lighting and shadow effects and very good sound effects combined with a minor level of strategy in the use of your rechargable flashlight give the game a really good edge. At times you will find yourself low on health prowling around with your flashlight looking for a medikit. The game recreates the feeling of arcade machines of old by giving you NO save points on levels. You start a level and finish it or next time start from the start. You have 5 retries/lives and this helps to create that arcade feeling by not letting you have unlimited retries. This however in itself i feel is the only real big letdown of the game. Although for some gamers this will make no difference it will make a big difference to the more casual gamer who isn't able to spend a long time scouring the levels looking for the extra weapons and ammo stashes that all games like this have. This means that as you progress further into the game you have to have more time to complete a level because if you dont finish that level in that sitting the next time round you have to start from the start of that level again. No checkpoints - no saves - only 5 retries per game. Despite this one annoying detail it is a really good game especially if you can get hold of the Shadowgrounds Pack (on sale at time of writing) for less that £2.00. This is a good game and the keyboard mouse controls work really really well on this game. A lot of games like this fail badly because of poor control system but the devs for this game have got this spot on for this game. This is also one of the reasons i can recomend this game. The controls feel very natural and you wont find yourself madly bashing buttons at anytime because the controls work well and feel intuitive after 5 minutes of playing the game. The different skill levels will provide a good challenge for more experienced players and the option of local coop make this game even more of a reason to buy it. Oh you actually read this far? Why? Just go buy the game - you will spend £2 on worse things in your life. Enjoy.

text: Shadowgrounds was the first game of Frozenbyte, the studio that gave us Trine and Trine 2. It's their first game, and although it has some weak points, they got the job reasonably well done. The story was surprisingly solid (at least until the last-level bug-hunt, which was a rather mundane dungeon-crawl) with some unexpected twists and decently capturing the feel of the cyberpunk genre. text: Just finished Shadowrun Returns, took just under 18 hours, excellent game. The story was better than the gameplay, there are just so many character options, it can be a bit overwhelming. Multiple races and multiple classes. Each race is built for one or two classes, otherwise you'll have a cap on how much you can invest into certain skills. For example you don't want to use a Troll for a charisma build, because they have a level cap on charisma early on, that would be better suited for an Elf, but the Troll would be good for a strength build. I played as an Elf and went charisma, it went well. I think it's probably the best choice I could have made, but I didn't use my Shaman class at all hardly, the magic in the game can be kind of pointless, but useful at times, but I found it generally easier to just shoot people in the face with a shotgun. You work with a team, which you pick every mission, they upgrade themselves overtime, you don't get to upgrade them, so the only customizable character is your own. However I found myself frustrated on multiple occasions when I would bring a Decker (tech person) and not be able to interact with tech objects as my personal skill was too low, despite having a qualified Decker attempting to interact with the object. So I missed some opportunities by not playing as a Decker. As a Shaman your base stat is charisma, meaning if you want to improve your skills you need to first boost charisma. This means youre dumping skill points here instead of intelligence for a Decker build for instance. Despite missing some opportunities, I feel like charisma was the best possible outcome. You are constantly interacting with other characters, having high charisma means easier time manipulating people, also you unlock ettiquites along the way. These ettiquites essentially allow you to know what to say to a certain type of people to get your way. For example, if you've unlocked the security ettiquite, your dialogs with security will go swimmingly compared to not having them. All things considered, I feel like there wasn't enough emphasis on the magic system, as I played through the game and pretty much overlooked it entirely, the gameplay was ok, a pretty generic turn based game, but the story was solid. I kept coming back for the story. You get multiple dialog options when interacting with other characters, I went for the snarky asshat approach to most situations. TL;DR: Gameplay is par, Some mechanics are easily overlooked, Story is on point. Buy it for the story, if you're on a budget but curious, look up the story or watch a playthrough. title: shadowrun: dragonfall - director's cut
text: Please note: I've played the original expansion for Shadowrun Returns, not the Director's Cut version. However, I imagine they are similar enough to write a reasonably accurate review. In short, this is one of the best modern day RPG's. A fantastic story, amazing turn-based combat system, great characters and real Shadowrun-atmosphere unlike in the original Dead Man's Switch campaign (here you actually do runs against different corporations and other enemy factions, many of them are optional). In the basegame (Dead Man's Switch), maps are linear and your character skills and stats are not utilized enough in dialogue, but in Dragonfall, both have been addressed incredibly well. There is also a nice variety of character interaction and optional side quests (you know, REAL side quests, not like thos in Dead Man's Switch). In many ways, this game reminds me of the games from the golden age of Bioware: Baldur's Gate, Neverwinter Nights, Knights of the Old Republic and Jade Empire. It has similarly deep characters with interesting backstories and well thought-out story. But the setting here in the Shadowrun universe brings one unique spice to the mix: the morality is not as bland and dated as good vs. evil, but rather Witcher-like shades of gray. Then we have the epilogue section, which, while short, fills in some background information and specifics about the story and leaves the player off with an exceptionally satisfying solution - or solutions, there are choices that matter in the game! Couple words of criticism, though... While Dragonfall improves many aspects from the original Dead Man's Switch campaign, like adding a proper save system, side-quests, characters, shadowruns and story, the Matrix part is still just another combat system with little to no variety or difference to the "real world" combat. Luckily, there are now almost no compulsory hacking sections, so, while a bit dissappointed, I don't think this is a big deal. If you are looking for a Shadowrun game with an interesting hacking system, try the SEGA Genesis version of Shadowrun instead. Short story short: buy it, play it! If there is even a chance that you might enjoy a good old-stylish RPG mixed with modern day UI and mechanics or turn-based tactical combat game similar to XCOM:EU, I am almost certain you are going to enjoy this one thoroughly. To me, it left such a deep impression that I just can't put into words. I used to play the SEGA Genesis version of Shadowrun, and before I played this, it was hands-down the best implementation of the classic tabletop RPG. Now it has been dethroned by Dragonfall, easily. 9/10, an instant classic and underappreciated RPG. Compared to mediocre Dead Man's Switch, this is a _huge_ improvement.
